newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George see merger cost savings soon.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George see merger cost savings soon.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Monday it expected to see most of the benefit of cost savings from its merger with Advance Bank Australia Ltd in the first two years of the merger takes effect.
"I expect to see the benefit of about 80 percent of the cost savings in the first 24 months of the merger," St George managing director Jim Sweeney told reporters.
St George said it expected achieve cost savings of about A$140 million from the A$2.6 million merger with Advance.
"We have a clear vision for the bank and that is to be a nationally based consumer bank in Australia," Sweeney said.
Sweeney said the enlarged bank would cater for small business and private client banking.
He said the banking market is likely to change after the result of the Wallis Inquiry into Australia's financial system as the country was still overbanked.
"This merger allows us to position the new bank to have enough balance sheet muscle to be able to compete more effectively with the larger banks," he said.

"I have some confidence that we will have some positive re-ratings over the next year or two," said Sweeney, in reference to ratings agency Moody's statement in October that it may upgrade the long-term ratings for the merged bank.
Sweeney said he was unconcerned about the fall in the St George share price, which has fallen from more than A$9 to its close of A$7.35 on Monday, down 11 cents on the day.

He said the fall was due to the diluction effect from the issue of new shares for the merger and the removal of the takeover premium. National Australia Bank Ltd was seen as a predator for St George with its 6.8 percent stake.
Sweeney said NAB's stake would reduce to around five and six percent of the merged bank. NAB has said it owns about three percent of Advance Bank.
Earlier, Advance Bank shareholders approved overwhelmingly the bank's plan to change its articles of association as a prelude to the proposed merger with St George.
The change in the bank's articles of association allows a single shareholder to own more than 10 percent of its shares.
The enlarged bank would have assets of about A$40 billion and be the fifth largest bank in Australia.
